messages:
jamie: Quick q — can we reduce control-plane telemetry coming from customer VPCs? Peering traffic is flooding CP metrics and we’re leaking tenant IPs into traces.

marta: Yep. Two rough paths: 1) tiny telemetry proxy in customer VPC (sidecar/agent) that scrubs IPs and emits labeled metrics, or 2) do sampling + redaction at regional gateway.

devin: Sidecar is nicer for privacy but adds ops burden for customers. Gateway sampling centralizes control but risks more PII staying in-cloud.

lina: If we choose sidecar, we can restrict labels to { tenant_id(hashed), svc_qualifier, region } and never emit src/dst IPs. Keep traces coarse-grained. :shield:

kevin: Can we rely on SNI to derive svc_qualifier? Some customers terminate or rewrite SNI (corporate proxies) so it’s brittle.

marta: Good call. Fallback should be ALPN + port mapping. Also allow an explicit header/token for agents we trust.

jamie: Ops wants per-endpoint latency histograms (useful for SLA investigations) without exposing tenant IP. That suggests a short-lived session label that’s opaque.

devin: Proposed solution: cp-telemetry-proxy (minimal binary) that registers session -> returns session_id. Metrics use session_id + tenant_hash + svc_qualifier. No IPs.

lina: session_id mapping stored in controlplane for short TTL and purged. We can reconcile metrics to models using route_hash -> model mapping.

kevin: Cross-account peering case: customer VPC <-> our account via peering/transit gateway. We can’t inject sidecars into customer accounts. How do we get labels?

marta: Options: 1) eBPF/redaction at our gateway to drop IPs and attach route_hash if available, 2) short-lived token exchange at connection bootstrap from customer agent to us.

jamie: Token exchange sketch: customer agent does small mTLS handshake to register the upcoming TCP session and gets back a telemetry token. Gateway attaches token -> metrics pipeline uses token lookup to resolve tenant.

devin: Avoid putting token in cleartext TLS fields. Use separate small mTLS RPC over controlchannel. Pseudocode: 
```
# register session metadata
POST https://cp-registry.redwood.internal/v1/register
Headers: Authorization: mTLS-client-cert
Body: {"conn_id": "uuid", "svc": "inference", "ttl": 60}
Response: {"telemetry_token": "tkn_...", "expires_at": 164...}
```

kevin: That looks doable. Gateway then reads telemetry_token from TCP metadata (connection-level) and emits metrics with token label. Token store must be highly available and fast.

marta: Edge case: customers using shared NAT will have a single IP for many tenants — token approach still needed to disambiguate. Also need RBAC: customers opt-in to provide token mapping.

ops-bot: Reminder: security review + compliance ticket required before any design that stores tenant identifiers (even hashed). Ticket: COMP-2026.

jamie: Next steps: spike two prototypes — A) cp-telemetry-proxy sidecar (local agent) that emits hashed labels, B) gateway token-exchange + ephemeral token store. Spike owners: @lina (sidecar), @devin (gateway). Can we target a short spike this sprint?

lina: I can take sidecar spike, 2d. Will do minimal binary and a dashboard proof-of-concept.

devin: I’ll do gateway token flow, 3d. Will measure additional latency and token store QPS.

kevin: Add a short doc section about ALPN/SNI fallback and what we’ll redact by default.

marta: Sounds good. Once spikes land we’ll present in arch sync and pick approach. :white_check_mark:
